title: Researchers design flexible, metal-free TADF molecules for efficient orange-to-red OLEDs
content: Researchers from Japan's University of Osaka, working with partners in Poland, Denmark and the UK, have developed metal-free orange-to-red TADF emitters that use through-space charge transfer (TSCT). Unlike earlier long-wavelength TSCT emitters, the new molecules are flexible and do not need a rigid structure to hold them in shape. OLED devices made with the new emitters glow at 598–624 nm and reach an external quantum efficiency (EQE) of up to 14.

title: OLED Emitter Systems, Part 2: Phosphorescence - 100% efficiency, still waiting on blue
content: The OLED emitter is the material at the heart of every pixel, the organic molecule that actually turns electricity into light. Everything else in the stack exists to deliver charge to it. The emitter is a key part in determining the display's color, efficiency and lifetime.

title: AI server tracker: Beyond GPUs, chassis, power supplies, rail kits and cooling capture a bigger growth story
content: Taiwan's AI server component suppliers are surpassing last year's revenue well before December. Eleven of the 13 companies tracked across chassis, power supplies, rail kits and thermal management had already exceeded their full-year 2025 sales in the January–October 2026 period, although October's results show differing shipment momentum.

title: Buima battery orders stretch six months as LEO projects advance
content: Buima Energy reported a slight month-on-month increase but a year-on-year decline in October 2026 revenue, as construction projects entered completion and acceptance phases while battery module shipments remained steady. The company said battery module order visibility has reached six months, with new low-Earth orbit (LEO) satellite projects for 2027 in development.

title: Samsung reportedly buys four silicon photonics patents from Rockley
content: Samsung Electronics acquired four US silicon photonics patents from UK-based Rockley Photonics in September 2026, South Korea's Shinailbo reported on November 11, citing US Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) records. The reported acquisition could strengthen Samsung's intellectual property portfolio in optical interconnect technology as it expands its silicon photonics foundry business to compete with TSMC.

title: Canon to launch KrF lithography scanner rated at 400 wafers per hour in December
content: Canon Inc. said on November 10, 2026, that it will launch the FPA-6400ES6a, a krypton fluoride (KrF) scanner for manufacturing memory and logic semiconductors, in early December 2026. The company's release gave no exact launch date, price, or shipment volume.

title: Samsung targets early 2027 for first 3D Cube-H design kit
content: Samsung Electronics aims to complete its first 3D Cube-H design kit, a hybrid copper bonding technology for vertically stacked logic chips, in early 2027, with prospective customer evaluations to follow, ZDNet Korea reported on November 10, citing an industry source familiar with the plans.

title: OpenAI 3Q26 revenue tops US$10B as losses persist
content: OpenAI's revenue reached US$10 billion in the third quarter of 2026, up nearly 50% quarter-on-quarter, driven by demand from enterprises and new model products. However, its adjusted operating loss widened to US$10.9 billion, while revenue remained below that of rival Anthropic.

title: Dynamic Holding posts record 3Q26 revenue and profit on mix, price hikes
content: PCB maker Dynamic Holding reported October 2026 consolidated revenue of NT$10.637 billion (approx. US$323.6 million), down slightly from NT$10.648 billion in September as extended holidays reduced working days, but up 70.3% from NT$6.245 billion a year earlier and the company's second-highest monthly figure on record.

title: Infineon says data center orders already exceed target as factory output sets ceiling
content: Infineon Technologies told analysts that demand is no longer what limits its growth. On a November 10 call to discuss its fiscal 2026 results, the German chipmaker said orders for its data center power products already exceed the close to EUR4 billion (approx. US$4.46 billion) of revenue it forecasts for fiscal 2027, and that how much of that it can book will depend on how fast its factories and outsourcing partners can ramp.

title: Ingentec revenue jumps 79% in first 10 months
content: Ingentec’s consolidated revenue reached NT$1.329 billion (US$40.4 million) from January to October 2026, up 79.32% from the same period in 2025. However, October revenue fell 8.59% month-over-month and 18.37% year-over-year to approximately NT$130 million as shipments of specialty gases to Japan, South Korea, and domestic customers declined slightly.

title: AI's grip on capacitor supply leaves consumer electronics facing steeper price hikes
content: Nichidenbo Corporation said successive AI server generations, designed for higher power consumption and voltages, are increasing demand for high-end capacitors offering high capacitance and resistance to heat and voltage. AI-related products now account for 55–60% of its revenue, up from about 40% in the first quarter, and could exceed 60% in 2027.

title: Infineon's record quarter shows power chips moving from cyclical recovery to AI-led growth
content: Infineon Technologies ended fiscal 2026 with its strongest quarter ever, and the shape of the result says more than its size: profitability rose much faster than sales, and the German chipmaker now plans for a year in which power supplies for data centers become one of its largest single businesses.

title: Samsung researchers and colleagues from Hanbat National University extend OLED lifetime by tuning the surface potential of the electron-blocking layer
content: Researchers from Korea's Hanbat National University, together with colleagues from the Samsung Advanced Institute of Technology (SAIT), have shown that tuning the electrical surface potential of a thin layer inside an OLED can reduce efficiency losses and extend the device lifetime. Using an electron-blocking layer (EBL) with an optimized negative "giant surface potential" (GSP), the researchers extended the device's LT95 lifetime by about 20%, from around 29 hours to 35 hours.
